tasks.description:
**Question.** Does subthreshold stimulation of a frontal eye field site raise the visual response of a V4 neuron whose receptive field matches the site? (Task structure only: the measure is the recorded V4 response.)

**What is on the screen.** A central fixation spot on mid-grey. After a [[param:baseline_hold]] baseline, a dark oriented bar (Michelson contrast [[param:bar_contrast]]) appears in the recorded neuron's receptive field, at the distracter site, or at both, at the preferred or orthogonal orientation; the bars stay 1.5-2 s.

**What the subject does.** Only holds fixation (eye tracker; leaving the window ends the trial). No saccade and no report. Holding to the end is paid.

**Varied.** Display (RF bar, distracter bar or both; preferred or orthogonal) and stimulation (on or off). 200-500 ms after bar onset a STIM_TRIGGER event goes out on stimulation trials for the lab's stimulator ([[param:stimulation.current_ua]], [[param:stimulation.train_ms]] train); control trials mark the same moment with CONTROL_MARK.

**Measured.** Nothing behavioural beyond fixation outcomes; the trigger and sync marks timestamp each trial for the lab's V4 recording.

**What it can and cannot show.** With a V4 recording and an FEF stimulator this structures the paper's comparison of V4 responses after the train with and without stimulation. On its own it can show nothing about gating. The receptive field, FEF site and current threshold come from mapping paradigms that are not built here.
notes: Paper: 1.5-2 s stimulus, trigger 200-500 ms after display onset, 50-ms train at the example site, 200 Hz biphasic pulses, 20 µA example current, ten trials per condition.
EXAMPLE site values (ASSUMED): RF centre (-7.8, -7.8) dva, 5-dva diameter, preferred orientation 45°, evoked-saccade endpoint inside the RF, 40-µA threshold. Enter each site's own.

ASSUMED: uniform draws of both ranges, the six-display set, bar 2.0 x 0.4 dva, dark polarity at 93% on mid-grey (luminance 0.018 of maximum), 0.2-dva spot, 1-dva window radius, 2-s acquisition, 500-ms baseline, 1-s interval.
Diagram shows the "both, preferred" display; the other five displays omit a bar or rotate both by 90°.
